review_note: Read test and helper. (b) The oracle is an independent base-R reimplementation of the 5-node adaptive Gauss-Hermite scheme (Golub-Welsch nodes from an eigen-decomposition, own mode and observed-information curvature, tensor grid), so criterion (1) is met for what it can show: Julia implements that quadrature scheme correctly (agreement 2.27e-13). I validated the oracle itself on Totoro against a 701 x 701 brute-force grid for one q=2 group: grid -18.03146, K=5 -18.03147, K=15 -18.03146, K=41 -18.03146 (logit); cloglog grid -13.52591, K=5 -13.52622, K=15 and K=41 -13.52591. So the 15-node value is effectively the exact marginal, and the 5-node (Julia) value sits 0.009 to 0.082 from it (logged: logit -1264.6033 vs -1264.5948; probit -1177.5697 vs -1177.5554; cloglog -1082.0848 vs -1082.0033). That gap is not misleading provided the claim is scoped to the 5-node scheme and is not called exact; it is small relative to the bug gaps (smallest 3.06, R = identity logit) but 80x larger than the stated 1e-3 tolerance for cloglog, so 'matches the exact marginal to 1e-3' would be false. The Julia fit ESTIMATES the correlation: cors are read from fit$corpars by coefficient name and used in R; flipping and R = identity each move the oracle by 3 to 34. Six row keys (logit, probit, cloglog x mu:I, mu:x1) match three fits, one (1 + x1 | id) block with sd formulas on both coefficients. Hashes match, HEAD matches, console log: 60 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors, 0 skips, live block ran. Totoro native skips; Mac log not rerun. Does NOT establish: agreement with the exact marginal likelihood or accuracy of 5-node quadrature (gap measured at one fixture each, up to 0.08); that the Julia estimates are the maximiser; calibration, coverage or SEs; other node counts; one fixture and seed per link.
